chunks.text: 44-year-old female, Homemaker, resident of Punggol, Singapore.
History of pneumonia resolved 5 years ago
Fractured right wrist 10 years ago, fully healed
Completed a course of Amoxicillin for a dental infection 2 years ago without issues
General Anesthesia with Balanced Technique, including Fentanyl, Propofol, and Sevoflurane; Muscle Relaxant (Rocuronium) for intubation and surgery

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms./Mrs. [Name]. I'm [Provider's Name], the anesthesiologist who will be taking care of you during your surgery today. I'd like to go through some questions to ensure we have all the necessary information for your safety. Is that okay with you?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, sure, doctor. I'm ready.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Can you please tell me a bit about your medical history, especially related to your current condition that requires a laparoscopic cholecystectomy?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Okay lah... I've been having stomach pains, especially after eating. The doctor said it's because of my gallbladder, so they decided to remove it. I think that's all, really.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: I see. Thank you for sharing that. Now, let's move on to your medications. I have in my records that you're on Metformin, Lisinopril, Atorvastatin, and Ranitidine. Can you confirm if you are still taking all of these medications as listed?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Ah, about the Ranitidine, doctor... I actually stopped taking it about six months ago because it was causing me some side effects. I'm not on any H2 blocker now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for clarifying that. It's important we have the most up-to-date information. Are you currently taking any other medications, supplements, or herbal remedies not listed here?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. Just the Metformin, Lisinopril, and Atorvastatin. That's all.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Now, regarding allergies, we have penicillin listed with a rash reaction. Are there any other allergies or reactions to medications or foods we should be aware of?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, just the penicillin. That's the only one.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia? If so, were there any complications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, this is my first time. I've never had surgery before.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright. Now, in terms of your current health, how would you rate your overall energy level and ability to perform daily activities? For example, can you climb stairs or walk for a certain distance without getting too tired?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Hmm, I can walk around, but sometimes I get a bit tired faster than before, especially with the diabetes and all. But I manage lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. It helps us understand your functional status. Finally, have you eaten or drunk anything since midnight? It's important for your safety with the anesthesia.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. I've been fasting since last night as instructed.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Well, I think that covers everything. Thank you so much for your time and for providing all this information. It's crucial for us to provide the best care possible. If you have any questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to ask.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Thank you, doctor. I feel more at ease now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] fentanyl fifty micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:07] rocuronium sixty milligrams for intubation

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] sevoflurane at one point five percent

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] two liters of lactated ringers administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:35] mean arterial pressure dropped to fifty five, gave phenylephrine point two milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [09:00] surgery completed, reversed with sugammadex fifteen milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm feeling a bit groggy, but okay. My tummy is sore, but I think it's manageable.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's expected after a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Can you tell me your pain level out of 10?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe a 4 or 5? It's there, but not too bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright, we'll keep an eye on that. Have you felt any nausea or vomiting since waking up?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, nothing like that. Just a bit of a dry mouth, but that's all.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. How's your breathing? Any discomfort or tightness in your chest?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I'm breathing fine. Just a bit tired from the anesthesia, I think.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: You were under general anesthesia with a balanced technique, including fentanyl, propofol, and sevoflurane. Do you remember anything from the operation?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, nothing at all. Just waking up here.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's normal. Given your BMI and diabetes, we'll monitor your sugar levels and blood pressure closely. Any other concerns for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all. Just want to go home and rest.

Hemodynamic instability (hypotension) as evidenced by intra-op drop in MAP to 55 requiring Phenylephrine, which may persist into post-op period due to residual anesthetic effects and fluid status.

Patient has a history of diabetes, managed with Metformin 500mg twice daily, and hypertension, managed with Lisinopril 10mg once daily and Atorvastatin 20mg once daily. Patient is allergic to Penicillin (rash).

Intraoperative concerns included a drop in mean arterial pressure to 55 mmHg, requiring Phenylephrine 0.2mg, and potential for residual neuromuscular blockade despite Sugammadex reversal. Patient experienced fatigue preoperatively, which may exacerbate recovery challenges.

Monitor for postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) due to multiple emetogenic agents used. Ensure close glycemic control due to diabetes. Watch for signs of residual neuromuscular blockade and manage analgesia carefully, as Fentanyl may not suffice for postoperative pain. Be alert for potential hemodynamic instability.
